terms.grammar: fistula, fistulae f., with the adjective spīritālis, spīritāle
terms.comment: A description of ours: no reference work has a word for a snorkel (Morgan–Owens has the heading “scuba diving, snorkeling” with no Latin under it; nothing in Traupman, Levi–Bini, or Andresian). Fistula is the classical word for a pipe or tube, and Pliny uses it of the blow-hole of a whale (Lewis & Short); spīritālis, “of breathing, of air”, is Vitruvius’s adjective (māchinārum genus spīritāle), and Lactantius calls the windpipe fistula spīritālis (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Fistulam in ōs pōne et per eam spīrā.
phrases.english: Put the snorkel in your mouth and breathe through it.

phrases.latin: Faciem in aquam dēmitte: vidē piscēs!
phrases.english: Put your face in the water: look at the fish!

sources: Lewis & Short: fistula · Lewis & Short: spiritalis
